When comparing our lady crab samples (including the redo of SSAJ33), we found there to be a clear divide between the ocellatus species that is commonly found in Woods Hole, and our samples’ sequence alignment. This points towards two possible hypotheses as to why this consistency within the sequences in our samples is seen across the board: 1) these samples are from a completely different species altogether or 2) this is a pseudogene, or a copy of the COI gene that has accumulated mutations over time and was better selected for by the primers during our PCR. The first hypothesis is less likely due to the morphological similarities observed within our specimens and the ocellate lady crab.

In the context of all the various crab samples however, they appear to be much more similar. It is very evident that you can bunch up the samples into specific species categories.
